chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'A man died and left behind his wife.' He said, 'The wealth is hers.' I said, 'A woman died and left behind her husband.' He said, 'The wealth is his.'

Because this report carries two meanings: one of which is what Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned, that it is applicable during the Occultation of the Imam, because the wife is only given one-quarter of her husband's inheritance if there is an Imam who takes the remainder; so if there is no Imam, the remainder is also hers. The other, which is preferable in my view, is that if the wife is a relative and there is no relative of his closer to her than she, she takes one-quarter due to marriage and the remainder due to kinship, and that which reveals what we mentioned.

(1057) 17 What Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated - from al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar al-Basri who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind a wife who was a relative, and he had no relative other than her. He said, 'All the wealth is given to her.'
And it indicates what we mentioned, that the wife does not deserve more than one-quarter in the absence of children, even if there is no relative there.

-(1058) 18 What al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated - from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Nu'aym al-Sahhaf who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr died and made me his executor and left behind a wife, and he left no heir other than her. So I wrote to Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) and he wrote to me, 'Give the wife one-quarter and bring the remainder to us.'

-(1059) 19 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza al-Alawi wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him): A freedman of yours made me his executor with one hundred dirhams, and I used to hear him say, 'Everything that is mine is for my master.' He died and left her (the freedman's wife) and did not command anything regarding it, and he had two wives. As for one, I do not know her location at this moment, and as for the other, she is in Qumm. What do you command regarding this one hundred dirhams? He (peace be upon him) wrote to me, 'See that you give these dirhams to the two wives of the man, and their right from that is one-eighth if he has a child, and if he has no child, then one-quarter, and give the remainder in charity to whome you know has need of it, if Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: How is a wife's inheritance share calculated when there are no other heirs or children?
ai.summary: This passage from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the jurisprudential debate regarding a spouse's inheritance share in the absence of children or other close relatives, specifically contrasting the view that the wife inherits the entirety during the Imam's Occultation with the opinion that she receives only the marital quarter while the remainder is distributed via kinship. The narrations highlight the practical application of these rulings by prominent Shia scholars like Al-Saduq and Al-Kulayni, demonstrating how the 'fourth' share is distinct from the 'kinship' share, a nuance critical to Shia inheritance law. It further clarifies that in cases of multiple wives, the estate is divided among them according to their respective shares, with the surplus allocated to charity, reflecting the comprehensive nature of Shia fiqh in handling complex familial scenarios.
